details:
First and foremost developers should understand why the community is upset In the sense that there was no warning to this decision so all users have gone into a panic and responded with only negativity. We all know mods are essential to some people so it’s not worth mentioning all that. 
The possible solution: 
-Create a new VRC+ that implements more then just avatar slots and a picture. Features that would be valuable that clients had like being able to see people you have blocked or teleporting for example. 
-Be transparent with the community when things will be released. Give a date so people know when things will be updated. Leaving everyone in the dark will only cause more to leave because in the past few years few things like mods have been added to the game. 
-Focus on the essential EMM/disability mods first. Text to speech, portable mirror, comfy menu, anti crash/frame saving, in depth audio adjusting, in depth IK tweaks not just a lock on the body ect. 
-Lastly creating a way for Linux users to play the game if you are taking away their means of getting on at all.
This update is supposed to keep us safer but you developers need to learn from this and understand that you need to give warning next time and start the conversation before implementing or it will cause everyone to be upset. Have things like these essential mods ready to be integrated before transitioning. Do better for the community and after a while if progress is made you will receive support again.
title: What I think vrchat devs should do
